title: Asa’s Final Years

questions.question: Who came up against Judah in the thirty-sixth year of Asa?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:1 (ESV): "In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah..."

questions.question: What city did Baasha build/fortify?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:1 (ESV): "...and built Ramah, that he might permit no one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah."

questions.question: To whom did Asa send silver and gold?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:2 (ESV): "Then Asa took silver and gold... and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Syria..."

questions.question: What did Asa ask Ben-hadad to do?
options: Break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:3 (ESV): "...go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, that he may withdraw from me."

questions.question: What did Asa do with the stones and timber of Ramah?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:6 (ESV): "And with them he built Geba and Mizpah."

questions.question: Who reproved Asa for relying on the king of Syria?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:7 (ESV): "At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him..."

questions.question: What army had escaped from Asa's hand because he relied on Syria?
options: The army of the king of Syria
questions.correctAnswer: The army of the king of Syria
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:7 (ESV): "...therefore the army of the king of Syria has escaped from your hand."

questions.question: For whose behalf does the LORD show Himself strong?
options: Those whose heart is blameless toward him
questions.correctAnswer: Those whose heart is blameless toward him
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:9 (ESV): "For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is blameless toward him."

questions.question: How did Asa react to Hanani’s words?
options: He was angry and put him in the stocks
questions.correctAnswer: He was angry and put him in the stocks
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:10 (ESV): "Then Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the stocks..."

questions.question: What happened to Asa in his thirty-ninth year?
options: He was diseased in his feet, and his disease became severe
questions.correctAnswer: He was diseased in his feet, and his disease became severe
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:12 (ESV): "In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa was diseased in his feet..."

questions.question: Who did Asa seek in his disease?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:12 (ESV): "...yet even in his disease he did not seek the LORD, but sought help from physicians."

questions.question: Where was Asa buried?
options: In the tomb that he had cut for himself in the city of David
questions.correctAnswer: In the tomb that he had cut for himself in the city of David
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:14 (ESV): "They buried him in the tomb that he had cut for himself in the city of David."

questions.question: What cities did the commanders of Ben-hadad conquer?
options: Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali
questions.correctAnswer: Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:4 (ESV): "...and they conquered Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali."

questions.question: What did they burn for Asa at his funeral?
options: A very great fire in his honor
questions.correctAnswer: A very great fire in his honor
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:14 (ESV): "...and they made a very great fire in his honor."

questions.question: What did Asa inflict on some of the people at the same time he imprisoned Hanani?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 16:10 (ESV): "...Asa inflicted cruelties upon some of the people at the same time."

key_verse_text: For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is blameless toward him. You have done foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars.
